answer: Each identity joins a spiral ring of strangers who pass a single lantern from hand to hand, one hop per epoch, and the lantern only moves when the next holder proves a live pulse: a heartbeat signed within a short window after a public beacon, matched by a quorum of ring members who witnessed the same beat. Rings spiral outward as members earn trust, so a lone operator cannot run many lanterns at once, since every fake identity needs its own live heartbeat, its own witnesses, and its own ring slot in the same narrow window. Sybils collapse under the cost of being alive everywhere at once.
